audits.claim: The advanced-pagination gate uses raw superuser and global-access flags rather than the endpoint's established administrator permission checks.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:69-73 gates on request.user.is_superuser and member.has_global_access, whereas src/sentry/auth/superuser.py:4-9 requires an active secondary session and organization.py:119-124 uses is_active_superuser. The member flag is independent of role (src/sentry/models/organizationmember.py:209,216), and is copied directly into the RPC member at src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/serial.py:47; the open-membership-derived access property in auth/access.py:420-431 is a different property from the one actually read here. Nevertheless OrganizationAuditPermission still controls access (organization_auditlogs.py:40), and both paginator paths use the same organization-filtered queryset (:48-50,78,87), so this gate mismatch does not establish an audit-log authorization bypass. It is a misleading/redundant eligibility rule rather than a separate demonstrated security defect.

audits.claim: The new safety comment is false because negative offsets in previous-page cursors still reach Django queryset slicing.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:53-59 accepts 0:-5:1 and :28-29 preserves its negative offset and previous-page flag. For an ordinary DateTimePaginator request, src/sentry/api/paginator.py:164,182-184 passes -5 unchanged to the queryset slice, which Django rejects, while api/base.py:535-541 catches only BadPaginationError from get_result. However HEAD^:src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-180 already sliced queryset[offset:stop] with that same negative value, so this is a pre-existing failure now incorrectly advertised as safe, not a newly introduced crash. The separate optimized-paginator branch in finding 2 also breaks forward cursors; this finding concerns the shared base and its inaccurate comment.

audits.claim: The added Cursor comment advertises new negative-offset support although the offset parsing and storage behavior did not change.
audits.evidence: src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-28 adds only the performance/support comment before self.offset = int(offset); HEAD^:src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 already had that assignment. Likewise head :53-59 and parent :51-57 both parse offsets with int without rejecting negatives, so this PR does not introduce parsing support. The promise of efficient reverse traversal is unsupported by src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184 and :877-882, which send negative previous/advanced offsets directly to Django slicing. The comment is misleading documentation; the underlying crash paths are separate findings, and forward negative offsets in the modified base are now clamped, so the finding's blanket statement about every queryset paginator is too broad.

audits.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result except for its negative-offset branch and therefore creates avoidable maintenance risk.
audits.evidence: Comparing src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845-911 with :136-215 shows identical cursor setup, limits, hit counting, ordering, cursor construction and post-query filtering, apart from comments and the advanced-negative-offset branch at :877-882. Its fallback slicing at :884-886 also matches the base at :182-184. If that branch is removed, the overridden get_result can be inherited without losing behavior; the subclass would still retain its constructor and key conversion methods (:834-843). This is real duplication and potential future drift, not an additional current functional defect.

audits.claim: The PR adds no tests for the optimized audit-log request path or the changed base-paginator offset handling.
audits.evidence: The supplied diff changes only src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py, src/sentry/api/paginator.py and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py, and a checkout-wide test search finds no optimized_pagination or OptimizedCursorPaginator references. tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_organization_auditlogs.py:22-49 covers ordinary requests with datetime rows but never selects the new path; tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py:143-153 checks negative offsets only for OffsetPaginator. A new-path test with one row would reach math.ceil(datetime) at paginator.py:838-840 through utils/cursors.py:121-122, exposing the conversion defect described in finding 0. This is a meaningful missing-test concern, distinct from the runtime defects it would catch.
